note: Demo quiz for a training session only. Each question is written from one IFANCA FAQ answer and quotes the sentence it comes from. Written for this demo, not by IFANCA. Needs review by IFANCA before any wider use.

items.question: According to IFANCA, what does the Arabic word halal mean?
items.source_quote: Halal is an Arabic word meaning lawful or permitted.

items.question: According to IFANCA, what is the opposite of halal?
items.source_quote: The opposite of halal is haram, which means unlawful or prohibited.

items.question: According to IFANCA, what does mashbooh mean?
items.source_quote: Such items are often referred to as mashbooh, which means doubtful or questionable.

items.question: According to IFANCA, what does Zabiha refer to?
options: Any meat sold in a Muslim country
Meat approved by a government inspector
Slaughtering of an animal or bird by a Muslim according to Islamic requirements
items.source_quote: Zabiha refers to slaughtering of an animal or bird by a Muslim according to Islamic requirements.

items.question: What mark do products certified by IFANCA normally display on the label?
items.source_quote: Products certified by IFANCA normally display the registered Crescent-M service mark on the label.

items.question: Why does IFANCA say lists of specific products are not as useful as ingredient lists?
options: Product lists are too long to read
The status of the products can change at any time
Product lists are only printed in Arabic
items.faq_question: What is the verdict on halal and haram lists?
items.source_quote: On the other hand, lists of specific products are not as useful because the status of the products can change at any time and this could lead to consuming haram products.

items.question: According to IFANCA, if the word gelatin appears on a label without its source, what is it generally derived from?
items.source_quote: If the word gelatin appears on a label without reference to its source, it is generally derived from pig skins and cattle bones, so it must be avoided.

items.question: Which label wording does IFANCA say halal consumers should look for on mono- and diglycerides?
items.source_quote: Halal consumers should avoid products containing mono- and diglycerides unless they are labeled as 100% vegetable mono- and diglycerides.

items.question: IFANCA says to check with the producer about lecithin unless the label says which words?
items.source_quote: Unless the ingredient label says soya lecithin or vegetable lecithin, you need to check with the producer to determine the source.

items.question: According to IFANCA, what is the active ingredient in rennet?
items.faq_question: What is the source of rennet?
items.source_quote: The active ingredient in rennet is chymosin.

items.question: According to IFANCA, what are Yellow No. 5 and other numbered dyes made from?
items.source_quote: Yellow No. 5 and all other numbered dyes (colors) are made from petrochemicals.

items.question: According to IFANCA, does chocolate liquor contain alcohol?
options: No, it does not contain any alcohol
items.source_quote: It does not contain any alcohol, so it is not haram.

items.question: According to IFANCA, how do Islam and Judaism differ on alcohol and wines?
options: Islam prohibits all intoxicants, and Judaism regards alcohol and wines as kosher
Judaism prohibits wine, and Islam allows it
items.source_quote: Islam prohibits all intoxicants, including alcohols, liquors and wines, whereas Judaism regards alcohol and wines as kosher.

items.question: How does IFANCA describe halal certification?
options: A qualified independent third party supervises the production of consumables
A label the company prints on its own
items.source_quote: Halal Certification is the process of having a qualified independent third party supervise the production of consumables, attesting that they were produced in conformity with the preparation and ingredient standards of the halal lifestyle.

items.question: Who makes all decisions related to halal certification at IFANCA?
items.faq_question: What is the procedure for suspension, withdrawal, reduction, maintenance, extension, or renewal of a halal certificate?
items.source_quote: The Halal Certification Committee is responsible for making all decisions related to halal certification including: granting, maintaining, renewing, extending, reducing, suspending, and withdrawing of halal certification.

items.question: According to IFANCA, does ISO 9000 on its own make a product halal?
options: Yes, ISO 9000 is the same as halal
Yes, if the plant is in the USA
No, ISO alone does not make a product halal
items.faq_question: How does ISO 9000 fit in with halal certification?
items.source_quote: ISO alone does not make a product halal, and a halal product can be made without ISO.

items.question: According to IFANCA, what meal classification do airlines currently use?
options: A Muslim meal rather than a halal meal
A certified halal meal on every flight
items.faq_question: May I eat the food served on airlines?
items.source_quote: The current classification includes a ‘Muslim’ meal rather than a halal meal.

items.question: What is the typical registration fee for a plant, as listed by IFANCA?
items.faq_question: What are the fees for certification?
